strings.d1.s0.name: Duomo di Milano
strings.d1.s0.tips: Gothic cathedral. Buy the combined ticket online (cathedral + rooftop, about 20 EUR) and arrive at the 09:00 opening, when it's quiet.
strings.d1.s1.name: Duomo Rooftop Terraces
strings.d1.s1.tips: Take the lift with the combined ticket. Walk among the spires; the Alps are visible on clear days.
strings.d1.s2.name: Galleria Vittorio Emanuele II
strings.d1.s2.tips: Glass-roofed arcade. Spin your heel on the bull mosaic for luck.
strings.d1.s3.name: Luini Panzerotti
strings.d1.s3.tips: Fried panzerotti since 1949. Just behind the Duomo, and the queue moves fast.
strings.d1.s4.name: Museo del Novecento
strings.d1.s4.tips: Twentieth-century Italian art. Look for the window with a view of the Duomo and Pellizza's The Fourth Estate.
strings.d1.b0.name: Camparino in Galleria
strings.d1.b0.tips: Campari bar since 1915. Come for an aperitivo.
strings.d1.b1.name: Palazzo Reale
strings.d1.b1.tips: Temporary exhibitions in the royal palace. An alternative to the Novecento.
strings.d2.s0.name: Cenacolo Vinciano The Last Supper
strings.d2.s0.tips: Leonardo's fresco. Visits are 15-minute slots, and online tickets sell out 3 months ahead (a guided tour alternative costs about 99 EUR).
strings.d2.s1.name: Santa Maria delle Grazie
strings.d2.s1.tips: Bramante's dome. This is the church that houses the fresco.
strings.d2.s2.name: Sforza Castle
strings.d2.s2.tips: The Sforza fortress. See Michelangelo's Rondanini Pietà; the courtyards are free.
strings.d2.s3.name: Parco Sempione
strings.d2.s3.tips: Park behind the castle, with the Arco della Pace.
strings.d2.s4.name: Trattoria Milanese
strings.d2.s4.tips: Risotto alla milanese and cotoletta since 1933. Close to the Duomo.
strings.d2.b0.name: Ratanà
strings.d2.b0.tips: Modern Milanese cooking in Porta Nuova.
strings.d2.b1.name: Triennale Milano
strings.d2.b1.tips: Design museum at the edge of the park. An alternative to the castle.
strings.d3.s0.name: Pinacoteca di Brera
strings.d3.s0.tips: Caravaggio, Raphael and Hayez's The Kiss. Quiet in the morning.
strings.d3.s1.name: Brera Streets
strings.d3.s1.tips: Cobbled artists' quarter. Walk Via Fiori Chiari; the botanical garden is free.
strings.d3.s2.name: Pasticceria Marchesi 1824
strings.d3.s2.tips: Prada's pastry shop on the corner of Via Monte Napoleone. Cappuccino and pastry.
strings.d3.s3.name: Quadrilatero della Moda
strings.d3.s3.tips: Via Monte Napoleone and its fashion windows.
strings.d3.s4.name: Villa Necchi Campiglio
strings.d3.s4.tips: 1930s Art Deco villa with garden and pool. Guided visits.
strings.d3.b0.name: Bar Basso
strings.d3.b0.tips: The bar where the Negroni Sbagliato was born. Come for an aperitivo.
strings.d3.b1.name: Museo Poldi Pezzoli
strings.d3.b1.tips: Private collection in a historic townhouse. An alternative to Villa Necchi.
strings.d4.s0.name: Fondazione Prada
strings.d4.s0.tips: Rem Koolhaas's gold-clad tower and contemporary art. Bar Luce (Wes Anderson) is on site.
strings.d4.s1.name: Bar Luce Fondazione Prada
strings.d4.s1.tips: Bar designed by Wes Anderson. Have a sandwich for lunch.
strings.d4.s2.name: Bosco Verticale Porta Nuova
strings.d4.s2.tips: Tree-covered towers and Piazza Gae Aulenti. Modern Milan.
strings.d4.s3.name: Navigli Canals
strings.d4.s3.tips: Walk along the Naviglio Grande. On the last Sunday of the month there is an antiques market.
strings.d4.s4.name: Navigli Aperitivo Mag Cafè
strings.d4.s4.tips: Canal-side aperitivo. Spritz plus buffet, a Milanese ritual.
strings.d4.b0.name: El Brellin Navigli
strings.d4.b0.tips: Canal-side restaurant in an 18th-century building. Dinner.
strings.d4.b1.name: Pirelli HangarBicocca
strings.d4.b1.tips: Kiefer's The Seven Heavenly Palaces. Free entry; an alternative to Prada.
strings.d5.s0.name: Varenna
strings.d5.s0.tips: 1 hour by train from Milan. Colourful houses and the gardens of Villa Monastero (10 EUR).
strings.d5.s1.name: Bellagio Ferry
strings.d5.s1.tips: Ferry from Varenna, out in the middle of the lake.
strings.d5.s2.name: Bellagio
strings.d5.s2.tips: The pearl of the lake. Stone-stepped lanes and the gardens of Villa Melzi.
strings.d5.s3.name: Ristorante La Punta Bellagio
strings.d5.s3.tips: At the tip of the promontory with lake views. Try the risotto with perch (risotto persico).
strings.d5.s4.name: Villa Carlotta Tremezzo
strings.d5.s4.tips: Take the ferry to the opposite shore. Botanical garden and sculptures; azaleas bloom in April and May.
strings.d5.b0.name: Bellagio Gelateria del Borgo
strings.d5.b1.name: Como and Brunate Funicular
strings.d5.b1.tips: Cathedral and funicular in Como. An alternative to Villa Carlotta.
strings.d6.s0.name: Bergamo Città Alta Funicular
strings.d6.s0.tips: 50 minutes by train plus the funicular. The walled upper town is a UNESCO site.
strings.d6.s1.name: Piazza Vecchia
strings.d6.s1.tips: Le Corbusier's "most beautiful square". Climb the Campanone tower.
strings.d6.s2.name: Basilica di Santa Maria Maggiore
strings.d6.s2.tips: Baroque interior and the Colleoni Chapel.
strings.d6.s3.name: Da Mimmo Bergamo
strings.d6.s3.tips: Casoncelli (Bergamo-style stuffed pasta) and polenta in Città Alta.
strings.d6.s4.name: Bergamo Walls Walk
strings.d6.s4.tips: 5 km along the Venetian walls with views over the plain.
strings.d6.b0.name: Pasticceria Cavour Bergamo
strings.d6.b0.tips: Try the polenta e osei dessert.
strings.d6.b1.name: Accademia Carrara
strings.d6.b1.tips: Painting gallery. An alternative to the walls.
strings.d7.s0.name: Monumental Cemetery
strings.d7.s0.tips: Monumental cemetery full of sculpture. Free, an open-air museum.
strings.d7.s1.name: Chinatown Via Paolo Sarpi
strings.d7.s2.name: Ravioleria Sarpi
strings.d7.s2.tips: Chinese-Italian dumplings, eaten on the street.
strings.d7.s3.name: Milano Centrale
strings.d7.s3.tips: Huge station from the Fascist era. The Malpensa Express takes 50 minutes: time to say goodbye.
strings.d7.b0.name: Pavé Pasticceria
strings.d7.b1.name: Mercato Centrale Milano
strings.note0: An ATM metro ticket costs 2.20 EUR, a day pass 7.60. The Malpensa Express from Centrale or Cadorna takes 50 minutes. The city centre is walkable.
strings.note1: Book Last Supper tickets online 3 months ahead (15-minute slots). Buy the Duomo rooftop combined ticket online.
strings.note2: Winter is 2-8°C and foggy. In December there is the Oh Bej! Oh Bej! market and the opening of the Scala season (7 December); January brings fashion sales. Como is quiet in winter.
strings.note3: An aperitivo costs 10-15 EUR for a drink plus buffet (18:00-21:00) in Navigli. Risotto alla milanese and cotoletta cost 20-30 EUR. Coperto (cover charge) is 2-3 EUR.
strings.note4: During Fashion Week (February/September) and the Salone del Mobile (April), hotels cost three times as much.
strings.note5: To tip, round up the bill. Coffee standing at the bar costs 1.30 EUR, at a table 4 EUR.
